To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a gas molecule diffuses into small void space of a non-poreous solid and induces the solid-state transformation to the low-density form, and that this phenomenon can be exploited to discover more porous materials.

the transformation from high to low-density form occurs through diffusion of gas molecules through the non-pore solid and into the lattice voids, followed by the transformation of the solid to a low-density kinetic form, and that this process is fully reversible.
gas molecules seem to diffuse into small lattice void spaces and initiate the transition of the high-density form of the non-porous p-tert-butycalix[4]aren to the low-density form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel materials for gas storage and separation.
the design and synthesis of novel porous materials with potential applications in gas adsorption and separation.
the synthesis, characterization, and gas sorption properties of porous organic frameworks (POFs) and metal-organic (MOF) frameworks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gas molecules diffuse into the solid and initiate the transformation, which is accompanied by the expansion of the lattice.
gas molecules diffuse through the nonporous organic solid and initiate the transformation to the low-density form.
the high-density guest free p-tert-butycalixarene undergoes a gas induced transformation to a low-density guest containing form, and that the transformation can be reversed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report the first example of a non-pore solid that can be reversibly converted to a porous solid by a gas molecule.
the gas molecules can induce structural transformation and expansion of the non-porous organic framework.
we have found a way to induce a transformation in a solid by the use of gas molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gas molecules may diffuse into the voids and induce a phase transformation that can be used to create new porous materials.
the gas molecule can be used as an effective agent for transforming the solid state of a material, and this transformation can be reversible, depending on the nature of the gas and the host solid.
a non-porous solid can be made to undergo a large volume change upon gas adsorption and release.
